sections.content: The specification defines Phase B/C evolution from a single-node prototype to an independently verifiable foundation. It covers server-controlled identity and account ownership, consistent private-resource isolation, OS-restricted Runner execution, versioned integrity-checked Workspace snapshots, durable restore attempts, compatible asynchronous resource state, and machine-verifiable evidence.
sections.title: Purpose and Capabilities

sections.content: The Phase service owns identity, ownership, scheduling, metadata, audit, restore orchestration, and stable APIs. Account is the tenant boundary and Browser is only a client. Deployment remains single-node with SQLite and local storage. Snapshots are explicit, immutable, path-independent, and exclude unsupported transient or sensitive project content. Restore and verification fail closed, project deletion is soft deletion, and retained data follows a 30-day single-node profile.
sections.title: Constraints and Scope

sections.content: Control-plane state may be cached for at most five seconds, with entry-boundary revalidation for new Runs, Restores, Previews, and private reads. Account disablement blocks new write leases and publication while atomic work drains or records a typed outcome. The baseline Windows profile assigns one restricted Runner identity per Project. The profile uses user-level actual-space quota, key references for encryption at rest, a fixture capped at 100 MiB and 10,000 files, and a 30-minute P95 restore-to-controlled-run target.
